data.name: Ajinkya
data.gender_notes: Ajinkya is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ajinkya is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘aj’ meaning ‘not’ and ‘inkya’ meaning ‘conquer’. This name is often given to a baby boy in Hindu tradition to signify that he will be invincible and unconquerable in his future endeavors. The name Ajinkya carries the meaning “Invincible, Unconquerable” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ajinkya usually hope their child will grow to embody invincible, unconquerable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ajinkya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Invincible, Unconquerable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ajinkya total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Ajinkya' has its roots in Sanskrit mythology and the Vedic tradition. It is a name that suggests strength, power, and invincibility, making it a fitting name for a child.

historical_references.reference: Ajinkya was a Maratha general and a strong commander in the army of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the founder of the Maratha Empire in India. He played a significant role in the Battle of Pratapgarh (1659) in which Shivaji was able to establish his de facto independence from the Mughal Empire.
historical_references.context: Battle of Pratapgarh, Foundation of Maratha Empire

historical_references.reference: Ajinkya was also a renowned poet and scholar. He composed several poems in Marathi language, especially on the goddess Amba, who is considered an aspect of Durga. Ajinkya's poems were published in the collections 'Ajinkyamaharasahasranam' and 'Ajinkyasatakam'.
